title: Certified Defense on the Fairness of Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: GNN prediction fairness can be corrupted by attackers that perturb input graph data.

gap.claim: The paper addresses the need to study certifiable defenses for GNN fairness.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes ELEGANT, a framework for certifiable defense of GNN fairness.
The paper presents a theoretical certification analysis for GNN fairness.
ELEGANT is designed as a plug-and-play framework that can use any GNN backbone without assumptions about its structure or parameters or requiring retraining.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper characterizes certifiable defense on the fairness level of GNNs as a novel problem.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report satisfactory practical effectiveness through extensive experiments on real-world datasets across different GNN backbones and parameter settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are prominent models for graph-based tasks.
Input-graph perturbations can corrupt the fairness of GNN predictions.
The paper studies certifiable defense for GNN fairness.
ELEGANT provides a theoretical certification framework intended to protect fairness under specified attacker perturbation budgets without backbone assumptions or retraining.
The authors report experiments on real-world datasets using varied GNN backbones and parameter settings.

source_observation.claim: A defense framework is described as applicable to any GNN backbone without retraining.

interpretation.claim: Compatibility and deployment effort are treated as design objectives alongside certification.

application.claim: When designing robustness mechanisms for existing models, favor interfaces that preserve the deployed model and minimize structural assumptions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the exact perturbation model, budget conditions, or applicability limits.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the fairness definition or protected attributes.
The abstract does not state the exact certification conditions or perturbation budgets.
The abstract does not identify datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
